title: How Deep Is Representational Bias in LLMs? The Cases of Caste and Religion
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures representational bias in Large Language Models, specifically quantifying the distribution of religious and caste representation in generated stories about life rituals (birth, wedding, death) in India and comparing this distribution against actual census data to identify underrepresentation and erasure of marginalized groups.
findings: The study found that GPT-4 Turbo exhibits severe representational bias concerning religion. Hinduism, the dominant religious group in India, was significantly overrepresented across all tested states and rituals in response to baseline prompts. Diversity-seeking prompts (using 'another' or 'a different' story) largely failed to correct this bias, with the skew towards the Hindu majority persisting. In one state (Odisha), diversity prompts shifted representation toward 'Other' (often tribal) religions but not Islam. This suggests a 'winner-take-all' dynamic where even a marginal statistical advantage for the majority group in training data leads to its overwhelming dominance in the model's output, indicating a deep-seated algorithmic bias rather than simple data scarcity.
